question.text: A gun of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi>kg</mi></math> fires <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn></math> bullets per second. The mass of each bullet is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>20</mn><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> and the velocity of the bullet, when it leaves the gun, is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>300</mn><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The force required to hold the gun while firing is

solution.text:
Rate of change of momentum of the bullet in forward direction = Force required to hold the gun.

F=nmv=4×20×10-3×300=24 N
